rules.text: Section 14(1)(b) permits recovery of possession on the ground that, on or after 9 June 1952, the tenant sub-let, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of the whole or any part of the premises without the landlord's consent in writing; subletting, assignment, and parting with possession are distinct concepts applying to different circumstances.

source_refs.quote: that the tenant has, on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;
These three expressions deal with different concepts and apply to different circumstances.

In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant and all the incidents of letting or tenancy have to be found, namely the transfer of an interest in the estate payment of rent, and the right to possession as against the tenant in respect of the Premises sublet.
In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.

The expression "parted with possession" undoubtedly postulates parting with possession session means giving possession to persons other than those to whom possession has been given by lease and "parting with possession" must have been by the tenant.
The divestment or abandonment of the right to possession is necessary in order to invoke the clause of parting with possession
without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;
If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself

So long as the lessee retains the legal possession of the whole of the premises he does not commit a breach of law against parting with the possession by allowing other people to use the same. A tenant cannot be said to part with the possession of any part of the premises unless his agreement with the license wholly ousts him from the legal possession of that part. IK-190902:L110.text: In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant and all the incidents of letting or tenancy have to be found, namely the transfer of an interest in the estate payment of rent, and the right to possession as against the tenant in respect of the Premises sublet. In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.

IK-190902:L111.text: The expression "parted with possession" undoubtedly postulates parting with possession session means giving possession to persons other than those to whom possession has been given by lease and "parting with possession" must have been by the tenant.

IK-190902:L112.text: The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself or in other words there must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession. The divestment or abandonment of the right to possession is necessary in order to invoke the clause of parting with possession: See cite11†Hazari Lal v. Gian Ram . 1972 Ren Cr 74 (Delhi).
